Cluster Overview

1. What is an Ignite Cluster?
  • A cluster is a group of Ignite nodes that have discovered each other and work together to store data, execute queries, and run compute tasks;
  • Every node in the cluster is aware of all other nodes (full topology awareness);
  • Nodes can be added or removed at runtime without stopping the cluster — Ignite automatically rebalances data;
2. Server Nodes vs. Client Nodes
Aspect Server Node Client Node
Stores data Yes No
Executes compute Yes Yes (delegates to servers)
Joins topology ring Yes Yes
Receives partition map Yes Yes
Configuration setClientMode(false) (default) setClientMode(true)
Use case Data storage, heavy processing Application entry point, streaming data in
3. How Nodes Form a Cluster
  • On startup, each node uses a discovery mechanism to find existing cluster members;
  • The discovery mechanism uses an IP Finder to obtain a list of addresses to try;
  • Once a node connects to any existing member, it receives the full topology and joins the cluster;
  • All nodes must use the same discovery configuration to find each other;
4. Cluster Topology Events
  • When a node joins or leaves, Ignite fires topology change events;
  • NODE_JOINED — a new node has joined the cluster;
  • NODE_LEFT — a node has gracefully left the cluster;
  • NODE_FAILED — a node has unexpectedly disconnected (crash, network failure);
  • Applications can listen for these events to react to topology changes;
5. Cluster States
  • ACTIVE — the cluster is fully operational; caches can be created, data can be read/written;
  • ACTIVE_READ_ONLY — the cluster allows reads but blocks writes; useful for maintenance;
  • INACTIVE — the cluster does not allow any cache operations; used when persistence is enabled and the baseline topology is not complete;
  • You can change the cluster state via the control script or programmatically: 
    ignite.cluster().state(ClusterState.ACTIVE);
